fieldContract.claims[]: Each entry is shaped to claimSchema in src/lib/content/schemas.ts, minus the lifecycle fields Codex owns (reviewState, publicationState, approvalManifestId, contentChecksum, review, history, relationships). Codex can split this array into individual claim records without inventing content.
fieldContract.claims[].id: Proposed lowercase kebab-case entity ID. Proposed, not authoritative: Codex owns content/claims/.
fieldContract.claims[].type: One of the eight master plan section 9.3 claim types.
fieldContract.claims[].statement: The claim as it would be rendered. Language is calibrated to certainty per master plan section 9.5.
fieldContract.claims[].plainLanguage: The same claim for a reader who has not opened a methodology paper.
fieldContract.claims[].scope: Population and conditions the claim is bounded to. A claim read outside its scope is a different claim.
fieldContract.claims[].qualifiers: Every limit that must travel with the claim. A confident sentence without these is a defect.
fieldContract.claims[].evidence: certainty, applicability, direction and magnitude, as four independent axes per master plan section 9.4.
fieldContract.claims[].sourceLinks[].sourceId: The proposedSourceId of the extraction that supports, qualifies or contradicts this claim.
fieldContract.claims[].sourceLinks[].locator: The exact place in that source. Every link has one.
fieldContract.claims[].sourceLinks[].supportStrength: direct, partially-direct, or indirect, for the claim being made rather than for the study in general.
fieldContract.claims[].recordIds: The screening-flow recordIds behind the sourceLinks, so a reviewer can walk back to retrieval.
fieldContract.absenceRecords[]: Not claims. Explicit records that the evidence did not support a claim, kept separate so an absence is never rendered as an assertion.

draftingRule: Every statement in the three content drafts is generated from this file. A sentence in a draft that is not traceable to a claim ID here, or to the draft's own explicitly labelled definitional or provenance sections, is a defect.

claims.statement: The pectoralis major arises from the anterior surface of the medial half of the clavicle, the anterior surface of the sternum, the upper costal cartilages and the aponeurosis of the external oblique, and inserts on the lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus.
claims.plainLanguage: The chest muscle runs from the collarbone, breastbone and upper rib cartilages to a narrow attachment on the upper arm bone.

conditions: gross anatomy of the intact muscle

qualifiers: The attachment description is taken from an authoritative reference chapter; the primary cadaveric studies in this evidence set measured the humeral end rather than re-describing the origins.
About a third of dissected specimens depart from this configuration in some way (see claim-pectoralis-major-structural-variation).

claims.statement: At the humerus the pectoralis major tendon has a tall, narrow footprint, measured in fourteen cadaveric specimens at 75 mm (SD 9) superior-inferior by 7 mm (SD 1) medial-lateral, with the clavicular head tendon shorter than the sternal head tendon.
claims.plainLanguage: Where the chest muscle attaches to the arm bone, the attachment is long from top to bottom but very narrow from side to side.

conditions: fresh-frozen whole upper extremities, imaged and then dissected

qualifiers: Fourteen specimens in one series; donor age and sex are not stated in the retrieved text.

claims.statement: In one cadaveric series using ultrasound, MRI and histology on the same fourteen specimens, the pectoralis major humeral enthesis was unilaminar and fibrocartilaginous in every specimen, and none of the three methods identified the tendon layers that the standard description reports.
claims.plainLanguage: A study that imaged and then sectioned the same fourteen shoulders found a single-layer attachment, not the two-layer attachment usually described.

conditions: the enthesis specifically, not the whole tendon

qualifiers: One series of fourteen specimens.
The finding concerns the enthesis; the authors are explicit that a layered structure elsewhere in the tendon is not excluded.
This contradicts the layered description repeated in reference works, and the contradiction is unresolved in the primary literature.

claims.statement: The pectoralis major is conventionally divided into a clavicular portion and a sternocostal portion, named for their origins, with an abdominal part described as a third division.
claims.plainLanguage: The chest muscle is usually described as having an upper part from the collarbone and a larger lower part from the breastbone and ribs, plus a small lowest part.

conditions: descriptive division of the intact muscle

qualifiers: The sternocostal head is described as having between two and seven distinct segments, so a two-part division is a simplification.
The abdominal part has its own traceable nerve supply, which supports treating it as a separable division.

claims.plainLanguage: Roughly one chest muscle in three differs in some way from the textbook description.

scope.population: 40 adult cadavers of both sexes, 22 male and 18 female

qualifiers: One cadaveric series; donor age is not stated in the retrieved text.

qualifiers: Moment arm is leverage, not force and not activation: a large moment arm does not by itself establish how much a muscle contributes to a given movement.

The shoulder was modelled as the humerus relative to the thorax with no separate scapula, which the authors name as their key limitation.
A joint moment is an external mechanical demand, not a muscle force and not a growth stimulus.

absenceRecords.interpretation: Absence of evidence, reported as absence. This is not evidence that the cable fly is ineffective, and it is not evidence that it is equivalent to a bench press. It means nobody in the retrieved literature has measured it.
absenceRecords.governingDecision: The frozen U2/EU2 decision forbids widening Y or pooling a related condition into the primary comparison. A later widening would require a dated scope amendment and a new search and could not become the primary result retroactively.
